title: Zerubbabel the LORD's signet ring (Hag 2:20–23)
speaker: The LORD through Haggai
description: The LORD will shake heaven and earth and overthrow the thrones and armies of the nations; on that day he will take Zerubbabel his servant and make him like a signet ring, for he has chosen him.
in_text_interpretation: The text gives no fulfilment. The signet image reverses Jer 22:24, where Coniah (Jehoiachin), Zerubbabel's grandfather, is torn off like a signet.

interpretations.label: Haggai expected Zerubbabel himself to become the Davidic king; the hope was not realised
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Zerubbabel is addressed by name, as "my servant" and "chosen", in a context of overthrown thrones; Haggai "identified Zerubbabel with the long-expected son of David". Historical evidence: Zerubbabel disappears from the record; no Davidic kingdom was restored under Persia.

interpretations.label: A promise to David's line through Zerubbabel, fulfilled in the Messiah
proponents: C. F. Keil (1868), after Koehler, Calvin and Osiander
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the signet reverses the rejection of Jehoiachin (Jer 22:24) and restores the Davidic line's standing; Keil applies it to Zerubbabel's position as representative of David's house rather than to his person. The New Testament genealogies include Zerubbabel (Matt 1:12–13; Luke 3:27). Objection: Mitchell reads the oracle as a concrete hope for Zerubbabel himself.

referents.referent: The Davidic line represented by Zerubbabel
